title: Ionic lattices: sodium chloride and caesium chloride
caption: In NaCl each ion has six nearest neighbours of the opposite charge (6:6), and the cubic cell holds four of each. The larger Cs⁺ fits eight Cl⁻ around it in CsCl (8:8). The cation-to-anion size ratio decides the structure.
alt: Two unit cells: sodium chloride, with alternating Na⁺ and Cl⁻ at every half-step; caesium chloride, with Cl⁻ at the corners and Cs⁺ at the centre.
description: Sodium chloride: ions alternate along every edge; each has six nearest neighbours of the other kind.
Caesium chloride: one Cs⁺ at the body centre surrounded by eight Cl⁻ at the corners.
